title: Weekend microburst causes soft-capacity drift and reserved-pool under-provisioning
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Summary: Over the weekend (2026-03-07 18:00 UTC -> 2026-03-08 06:00 UTC) several customers experienced degraded throughput and intermittent 429s despite apparent free headroom in our reserved pools. This ticket tracks the investigation, short-term mitigations, customer comms, permanent fix, and follow-ups.

Observed behavior: Dedicated tenant requests were frequently routed to cold pools or rejected with burst-limit errors during 10-30s microbursts. Autoscaler did not replenish reserved capacity in time due to a deficit in the headroom signal derived from the epoch lease table and a smoothing heuristic that suppressed scale-ups during short bursts. Customers affected include multiple mid-market tenants with bursty traffic patterns; highest-severity reports came from AcmeHealth (support case #ACM-4782).

Impact: Increased 429s and degraded p50/p95 latency for bursty traffic, leading to customer escalations and rollback requests. Estimated customer downtime-equivalent: partial degradation for ~3 hours for five tenants.

Hypothesis (root cause): The autoscaler smoothing window with a 5-minute decay and our epoch lease TTL updates were interacting such that short microbursts were averaged out, leaving the headroom predictor under the actual instantaneous demand. Additionally, a race in lease-table cleanup (slow compaction during weekend maintenance window) caused transient stale headroom metrics reported to the scale controller. Together these caused scale-ups to be postponed until the burst ended.

Why this is unique/different from previous incidents: Unlike classic warmup starvation, the system showed nominal reserved-pool capacity and correct token accounting—yet routing logic preferred cold pools because the controller flagged predicted future saturation based on stale metrics. Previous tickets focused on burst-credit accounting bugs; this one is primarily a telemetry/aggregation latency + smoothing hyperparameter interaction that masks short bursts.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Diego Morales: Initial triage complete. Reproduced in staging with synthetic microburst generator (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscale-sims PR #142). Observed same headroom decay behavior. Added short-term mitigation: reduce smoothing alpha to 0.3 on the canary autoscaler.

2026-03-11 - Anika Shah: Deployed canary to us-west-2 dedicated cluster at 09:20 UTC. Preliminary metrics: 40% reduction in 429s for synthetic bursts of 30s. Not safe to roll cluster-wide without further testing because this increases oscillation risk for noisy tenants.

2026-03-11 - Leah Park (SRE): Ran failure-injection tests to validate warmup protections remain (linked runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/Autoscaler-Warmup-Runbook). Observed no adverse evictions under 20% additional churn. Recommended add guardrail: min_cooldown_ms = 300k.

2026-03-12 - Product (Maya Singh): Customer comms draft ready for AcmeHealth; recommended ETA for broader mitigation: 48-72 hours. Shared dashboard showing customer impact and mitigation progress: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/incident/ENG-2718281

2026-03-13 - Anika Shah: Root cause narrowed to two contributors: (1) lease-table compaction lag during weekend maintenance; (2) smoothing-window alpha too aggressive for <2m bursts. Created PR with changes: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/187 (patch: prefer recent max-quantiles over moving average for short-window signals).

2026-03-14 - Diego Morales: Security review not required. Coordination note: Private deployments (on-prem agent) will need an equivalent patch but we cannot auto-upgrade customers; flagged for solutions team.

2026-03-15 - Anika Shah: Planning permanent rollout. Steps: a) merge PR #187 after safety tests; b) release runtime flag 'short_burst_mode' default off for Dedicated; c) enable for 20% of tenants + monitor for oscillation for 48h; d) broader enable if stable. Preparing postmortem and changelog entry.
